newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria issues 7-yr bonds to guarantee deposits.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria issues 7-yr bonds to guarantee deposits.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry issued 30.552 million levs of seven-year floater coupon bonds to cover payments to depositors in banks that the central bank seeks to close down, the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said.
The bonds bear a semi-annual coupon equal to the BNB's central interest rate (CIR) for the period to maturity, the BNB said in a statement.
The CIR is now set at 18 percent monthly or 216 percent annually. Principal payments are due in seven equal annual installments until maturity.
The paper was placed with the State Savings Bank (SSB), which in mid-July began to repay lev deposits in five local banks against which the BNB has filed insolvency suits.

The issue was dated June 27, 1996 but the statement was released now because the ministry had calculated the par value on the basis of SSB data on actual payments made to depositors and creditors of the five banks so far, a BNB official said.
The new issue is the sixth one of this kind. It brings to 19.482 billion levs the total par of deposit guarantee seven-year T-bond issues placed with the SSB since mid-1996.
